release: MINOR, additive, and it only ever ADDS coverage: the Content & SEO tab can now answer "can Google and Bing actually index this?" per URL. Eleven new scored rules join the seo suite (SEO-039..049) plus advisory Suite 14 Discovery & AI (DISC-001..006, WEIGHTS.discovery = 0, every row manual). Scores are comparable in MODEL but not in VALUE across this boundary — the seo denominator grew, so a site with a clean sitemap scores slightly higher and one that publishes URLs it forbids scores lower. Nothing was removed and nothing was reweighted. WHAT IT SEES THAT NOTHING DID BEFORE: every input was already fetched and every signal was already checked in isolation — SEO-007 sees noindex, SEO-020 sees a blanket robots block, SEO-023 sees dead sitemap URLs. The defect class lives in the INTERSECTION, which no single-signal rule can reach: a URL the sitemap advertises, that robots.txt forbids, carrying a noindex the crawler will never be allowed to read (SEO-047). SEO-048 is the companion case SEO-020's site-level boolean cannot express — `*` open while a group NAMING googlebot or bingbot closes that one engine, so a site is indexable in Bing and invisible in Google and the blanket check calls it clean. robots.txt is now parsed per RFC 9309 (longest-match group selection, wildcards, Allow-wins ties) instead of file-wide regexes. THE BOUNDARY, STATED: this ships INDEXABLE, never INDEXED. Live index membership needs a credentialed, ownership-verified API per engine, and scraping site: queries is non-deterministic and against both engines' terms, so indexStatus.measured is false with its reason attached to the data — no surface can render the verdict table as "indexed in Google". THREE DEFECTS THIS PASS CAUGHT IN ITSELF, none of which the unit tests would have found. First, allows() was called with the bare path '/' and new URL('/') throws, so a robots.txt that closed the whole site to Googlebot reported it as crawlable — the exact false green the module exists to prevent. Second, on a DEAD host the crawl-gate row minted the green "Google and Bing can crawl the site": unreachable robots.txt answers "nothing is forbidden", which is right for a live site and catastrophic for one nobody could reach. Third, measured on a real site where every unknown path answers 301 to a 404 page, "absent" arrived as a REDIRECT and both the sitemap and well-known probes read it as present-and-broken — the report claimed four machine-readable files the site does not have, each with a defect it does not have. Absent now covers redirect, empty body and HTML shell. Also: the single-page contract was violated and is now enforced end to end — a "This page" run was HEAD-probing sitemap URLs, fetching three pages the operator had just scoped out. TAB ORDER: the two single-site tools now sit together — 1 Site Audit, 2 Content & SEO, 3 Visual Comparison, 4 Post-Deployment Check, 5 Reports. Every tool keeps its own separate Settings gear.
